correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the published 12-vertex triangulation from its four symmetry generators and three facet seeds. The resulting order-24 action gives 48 tetrahedra, 96 triangles and 60 edges. Independent GF(2) row reduction gives ranks 48 for cocycle equations and 11 for vertex coboundaries, hence dim H^1(F2)=1 and 2048 representatives in its nonzero coset. Independent exhaustive enumeration reproduces exactly the ten weights 21:60, 23:132, 25:144, 27:240, 29:360, 31:408, 33:400, 35:240, 37:60, 39:4. Reconstructed local 1|3/2|2 tetrahedral cuts, with 36 minimum cocycles of disk profile (20 triangles,10 quadrilaterals) and 24 of (18,11); read the submitted checker’s connectedness and chi=1 tests and the proof of the converse for arbitrary normal RP2 using mod-2 intersection parity and Poincare duality. Weight>=support gives the universal lower bound, equality requires exactly one intersection on active edges, hence no missing multi-normal representatives. Finite enumeration is genuinely exhaustive on this one triangulation; it does not establish claims for arbitrary triangulations.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: The Köhler-Lutz primary 2005 classification gives this exact vertex-transitive 24-cell quotient, incidence structure and symmetry group but does not report normal RP2 intersection systoles or the full nonzero H^1 cochain weight enumerator. A directly related Resultary record for the identical complex classifies shortest essential integral H1 triangular loops (64 in 4 orbits), a different primal invariant that does not imply the dual cocycle minimum or 60 projective planes. Normal-surface dualization itself is standard and not claimed new; the exact 21 bound, 60 minimizers, orbit decomposition and local disk profiles are the additional exact findings. Historical unindexed normal-surface computations remain a risk.

value.rationale: PASS: A precise optimal normal projective-plane weight and complete minimizer/orbit classification for a natural highly symmetric triangulation of RP3 is a motivated triangulation-dependent normal-surface/coding-theoretic invariant, not merely a renamed topology fact. The weight enumerator and normal disk profiles distinguish configurations invisible to the previously known shortest H1 layer. It supplies an exact benchmark for normal-surface enumeration and cosystolic optimization; no invariance under changes of triangulation is asserted.

limitations: Result restricted to Köhler-Lutz labelled 12-vertex RP3 triangulation, embedded normal RP2 and total edge intersections counted with multiplicity.

Independent recomputation establishes the weight enumerator and disk counts; the group orbit/connectedness details were inspected in the original exact checker rather than independently exhaustively reprogrammed.
Published normal surface theory supplies the duality, but an older unindexed table might independently contain these numerical minima.
